First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1+2x+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (1+{tan}^{2}⁡x+2x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int ({sec}^{2}⁡x+2x)\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x+{x}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$
